programmes.d: Jokes are the theme on this show, with Martin Short, Terri Garr, and Michael Keaton. Lotsa fun!

programmes.t: The Best of the Dean Martin Show
programmes.d: Sketches and songs with Dean Martin and celebrity guests Bob Newhart and Sid Caesar.
Carol's guests are Soupy Sales and Gloria Loring. Loring teams up with Carol and Vicki for a spoof of "Valley Of The Dolls." Then, Sales and Carol play naive newlyweds on a most awkward honeymoon.
Carol's guests are the always funny Martha Raye and Mel Torme! Martha and Carol are rival artists in "The Sunday Painters". Then, Mel and Martha join the gang for a series of commercial parodies.

programmes.d: Please welcome Ms. Betty White to the stage! Betty plays Eunice's sister as 'The Family' celebrates Mama's birthday
For Carol's second season premiere, Jim Nabors and Alice Ghostley guest star! Alice plays Roger's sister in "Carol & Sis", and Jim has a most unusual blind date with Carol.

programmes.d: Tonight's guest star is the fabulous Cher! Sketches include Harvey and Tim as dueling pianists
Tonight: Vicki plays an author whose changes to her story are acted out by her characters, and Tim demonstrates the latest in safety for medicine bottles.

programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents Pearl Bailey, Buck Owens, Lucho Navarro, Petula Clark, David Frye, Trio Rennos, and The Band.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Carol's guests are Mickey Rooney and John Davidson!
The first actor to refuse an Oscar, George C. Scott for the title role in Patton, chats about his love of theatre, the many bombs in which he’s appeared, and turning 60 years old.
Mel Torme and Martha Raye are tonight's guests! Sketches include Martha and Carol as two dog-loving ladies, and spoofs of two Disney classics: "Sleeping Beauty" and "Mary Poppins."
Tonight's big guests are James Garner, George Carlin, and Ken Berry, who join Carol, Vicki, and Tim for an evening of can't-miss comedy.
Susan Sarandon, Brooke Shields, and Carol Wayne all stop by the couch, and Johnny talks about Playboy.
Tim Conway is Carol's guest for a sketch where a betrothed couple elect to paint their future home--with messy results. And in "Carol & Sis", a nervous Carol waits up for Chris to return from a date.
TV’s ultimate GOAT Carl Reiner performs a dance number then chats about writing screenplays and (wait for it) the Supreme Court.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Guests Ronnie Schell and Vicki Carr take to the stage with stand-up and song (respectively)!
Even stars get stiffed. Ask Bruce Dern. Comedian Robert Klein reports on making a movie with Burt Reynolds, and Dr. Carl Sagan bashes Star Wars for strangling science.
Actor/screenwriter Peter Fonda opens up about being compared to his father and sister. Charles Nelson Reilly recalls his dad pouring cheap bourbon into fancy bottles to hide their poverty.
Ed Begley Jr. returns and is joined by Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom's Kate Capshaw and comedian Bobby Kelton.
Lily Tomlin describes her Detroit childhood, creating a character by working a check-out counter and her career as a shoplifter.
Celebrate New Year’s day with Foster Brooks, Victor Buono, and…..Joan Embery and her gorilla friends.
Garry claims that he bombed during his previous appearance so this time he delivers the goods, covering everything from Sonny Bono to Captain & Tenille.
Oscar winner Jimmy Stewart describes an evening at the celebrity-fave nightclub when teenager Judy Garland showed up and sang for the gang.
Life is a cabaret when Joel Grey and Vincent Price are guest starring! The two play guests at a hotel where Carol is the switchboard operator (who listens in on all the calls.) Also: "Carol & Sis."
Rocky star Sylvester Stallone brings his son Sage to meet Johnny. Describes getting kicked out of several schools, and chats about stardom with fellow guest Steve Martin.
Ed Sullivan presents performances by The Young Rascals, The Turtles, Spanky & Our Gang, The 5th Dimension, Oliver, and The Beach Boys.
Was Richard Pryor’s grandmother really a tyrant? Hear Pryor’s recollections of grandma battle-ax. Comic genius Tim Conway remembers his early days in Vegas.
Full House dad Bob Saget explains his attempts at trying to improve his appearance. He also comments on the various people he meets at his gym.
